svg.title: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate: MegaLinter's reports belong to the developer who ran it, and to no one else
svg.text: a freshly generated project passes its own quality gate
Scenario: MegaLinter's reports belong to the developer who ran it, and to no one else

g.text: Given a generated project where MegaLinter runs only yamllint on its own
settings
The developer is bootstrap, an ordinary user without administrator rights. The last lines of
the project's MegaLinter settings keep one check, yamllint, on the MegaLinter settings files
only, so that a run takes seconds. PRE_COMMANDS: [] skips the spelling dictionaries
MegaLinter would install first.
ls finds no megalinter-reports folder yet: every report on the next cards comes from the run
shown there.
Then task megalinter:npx leaves reports only the developer can read or
change
task megalinter:npx is the run behind task devsecops:code. MegaLinter runs as root in its own
container and writes its reports straight into the project. The task's last step, in green,
gives them to the user who ran it with chown, then takes every right away from everyone else
with chmod -R go-rwx.
find lists each report with its rights, its owner and its group. Every line reads bootstrap
bootstrap. In drwx------ and -rw-------, the letters are bootstrap's own rights to open, read
and change, and the dashes after them mean nothing for anyone else.
And the developer can delete those reports without administrator rights
rm -r removes the folder and every report in it with bootstrap's own rights, without sudo,
and ls confirms it is gone.
Then task megalinter leaves its reports to the developer alone too
task megalinter, the usual way to run MegaLinter on a computer, runs it in Docker on a copy
of the project, then copies the reports back as bootstrap. Its last step, in green, is chmod
-R go-rwx megalinter-reports.
find shows the same rights as after task megalinter:npx: bootstrap bootstrap on every line,
and nothing for anyone else.

text.tspan: task megalinter 2>&1 | tail -n 5; find megalinter-reports -printf '%M %u %g %p\n' | sort

svg.text: Storyboard e2e · 4 steps · 4 frames · every frame is its own pixel baseline (tolerance: 0)
